text:
Taylor Hall played his 1,000th NHL game on Thursday, in Finland of all places, with the Hurricanes wearing his 71 in warmups at the Global Series. It capped a strange first month: an upper-body injury knocked him out on Oct. 13 after barely four minutes of ice time, and he did not return until Nov. 5.

The hockey around the milestone is better than the box score. He has 7 points in 12 games on about 13 minutes a night, but Carolina is getting 67% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly 9 points better than without him. His own chances are up to 1.35 expected goals per 60 from 0.90 last season. He is shooting 10.7%, the bottom of our range, and his linemates have finished 3.5 goals below their chances.

Context matters, and Evolving-Hockey supplies it: he plays with strong teammates (96th percentile), which flatters those on-ice numbers, though even adjusted they had him in the 91st percentile at driving play. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking calls him a setup man. At 35 and a Cup champion, the question is minutes, not ability.
